skill-snapshot-1ae6808a313e69faf5c5.exact_text:
---
name: snpeff-annotation
description: Build or use snpEff databases and annotate VCF variants with ANN effects. Use when the user asks for SNP/indel functional annotation with snpEff, including existing pre-built databases, custom GFF3/GTF/GenBank database builds, ANN interpretation, summary HTML, and safe database/version selection. Do not guess species databases, genome-version names, chromosome names, codon tables, or unchecked-build options from taxonomy labels alone.
metadata:
  domain: genomics
  summary: >-
    Annotate variants from an existing VCF against a reference genome and gene
    annotation to predict affected genes and variant effects.
  aliases:
    - variant annotation
    - variant functional annotation
    - variant effect annotation
    - SNP annotation
    - 突变功能注释
    - 变异功能注释
  task_types:
    - variant_annotation
    - variant_effect_annotation
  inputs:
    - variant_vcf
    - reference_fasta
    - annotation_gtf
    - annotation_gff3
    - annotation_genbank
  when_to_use:
    - An existing VCF needs gene and functional effect annotation.
    - A VCF must be annotated against a matching custom FASTA and GTF or GFF3.
  when_not_to_use:
    - Raw reads still require variant calling before an annotation-ready VCF exists.
  renderer:
    legacy_only: true
    execution_contract: legacy_renderer_v1
    renderer_id: genomics.snpeff_annotation
    entrypoint: scripts/render_snpeff_annotation_scripts.py
    runner: controller_python
    manifest_filename: manifest.json
    manifest_type: renderer_artifact_contract
    schema_version: 3
    composite_step: true
    task_spec_rules:
      - rule_id: snpeff.custom_database.typed_inputs.v1
        semantic_key: required_behavior.database_source
        role: database_source
        operator: eq
        value: custom_genome
        strength: hard
        level: required
        when_all_input_roles: [variant_vcf, reference_fasta]
        when_any_input_roles: [annotation_gtf, annotation_gff3, annotation_genbank]
    owned_outputs:
      - annotated.vcf
      - snpEff_summary.html
      - ann_effect_summary.tsv
      - ann_gene_summary.tsv
      - report.md
      - reproduce.sh
      - stage_status.tsv
    output_bindings:
      annotated_vcf: {mode: argument, argument: output_vcf, filename: annotated.vcf}
      snpeff_summary_html: {mode: fixed, filename: snpEff_summary.html}
      ann_effect_summary_tsv: {mode: fixed, filename: ann_effect_summary.tsv}
      ann_gene_summary_tsv: {mode: fixed, filename: ann_gene_summary.tsv}
      report_md: {mode: fixed, filename: report.md}
      reproduce_sh: {mode: fixed, filename: reproduce.sh}
      stage_status_tsv: {mode: fixed, filename: stage_status.tsv}
    invocation:
      binding_rules:
        genome_version:
          owner: generate
          repair_target: generated_action.produced_bindings.genome_version
          sources:
            - {kind: explicit_produced_binding, role: genome_version, rule_id: snpeff.genome_version.generated.v2}
      arguments:
        vcf: {flag: --vcf, required: true, aliases: [variant_file]}
        genome_version: {flag: --genome-version, required: true}
        outdir: {flag: --outdir, aliases: [output_dir], top_level: true}
        output_vcf: {flag: --output-vcf}
        snpeff_jar: {flag: --snpeff-jar, runtime_binding: SNPEFF_JAR}
        snpeff_command: {flag: --snpeff-command}
        java_options: {flag: --java-options}
        config: {flag: --config}
        data_dir: {flag: --data-dir}
        reference_fasta: {flag: --reference-fasta}
        annotation_gff3: {flag: --annotation-gff3}
        annotation_gtf: {flag: --annotation-gtf}
        annotation_genbank: {flag: --annotation-genbank}
        genome_name: {flag: --genome-name}
        cds_fasta: {flag: --cds-fasta}
        protein_fasta: {flag: --protein-fasta}
        config_line: {flag: --config-line, repeatable: true}
        allow_unchecked_build: {flag: --allow-unchecked-build, boolean: true}
        compress_output: {flag: --compress-output, boolean: true}
      routed_arguments:
        annotation_file:
          selector: annotation_format
          routes:
            "-gtf22": annotation_gtf
            gtf22: annotation_gtf
            "-gff3": annotation_gff3
            gff3: annotation_gff3
            "-genbank": annotation_genbank
            genbank: annotation_genbank
      runtime_only_arguments: [java_home]
      controller_owned_arguments: [producer_step_id]
  outputs:
    - {output_id: annotated_vcf, default_filename: annotated.vcf, format: vcf}
    - {output_id: ann_summary, default_filename: ann_summary.tsv, format: tsv}
    - {output_id: report, default_filename: report.md, format: markdown}
    - {output_id: reproduce_script, default_filename: reproduce.sh, format: bash}
    - {output_id: stage_status, default_filename: stage_status.tsv, format: tsv}
  generate:
    binding_contract:
      schema_version: 1
      public_input_protocol: public_handle_v2
      operations:
        prepare_database:
          produces_bindings: [genome_version, snpeff_db]
          consumes_bindings: []
          binding_types:
            genome_version: string
            snpeff_db: artifact_ref
          artifact_binding_requirements:
            snpeff_db:
              canonical_resource_id: artifact.snpeff_data_dir
              resource_kind: mutable_workspace
          required_binding_env:
            GENOME_VERSION: {source: produced_binding, name: genome_version}
            SNPEFF_DB: {source: produced_binding, name: snpeff_db}
        build_database:
          produces_bindings: []
          consumes_bindings: [genome_version, snpeff_db]
          binding_types:
            genome_version: string
            snpeff_db: artifact_ref
          artifact_binding_requirements:
            snpeff_db:
              canonical_resource_id: artifact.snpeff_data_dir
              resource_kind: mutable_workspace
          required_binding_env:
            GENOME_VERSION: {source: accepted_binding, name: genome_version}
            SNPEFF_DB: {source: accepted_binding, name: snpeff_db}
        annotate_variants:
          produces_bindings: []
          consumes_bindings: [genome_version, snpeff_db]
          binding_types:
            genome_version: string
            snpeff_db: artifact_ref
          artifact_binding_requirements:
            snpeff_db:
              canonical_resource_id: artifact.snpeff_data_dir
              resource_kind: mutable_workspace
              required_state: snpeff_database_ready
          required_binding_env:
            GENOME_VERSION: {source: accepted_binding, name: genome_version}
            SNPEFF_DB: {source: accepted_binding, name: snpeff_db}
      derived_artifact_layout:
        data_root: "<snpeff_db artifact>/data"
        genome_fasta: "<data_root>/genomes/<genome_version>.fa"
        annotation_gtf: "<data_root>/<genome_version>/genes.gtf"
        predictor: "<data_root>/<genome_version>/snpEffectPredictor.bin"
    execution_capabilities:
      - capability_id: genomics.snpeff_annotation.check_contig_compatibility
        operation: check_contig_compatibility
        required_runtime_binding_ids: []
        optional_runtime_binding_ids: []
        required_artifact_binding_ids: [artifact.variant_vcf, artifact.reference_fasta, artifact.annotation_gtf]
        consumes_artifacts: [artifact.variant_vcf, artifact.reference_fasta, artifact.annotation_gtf]
        produces_artifacts: []
        produces_bindings: []
        produces_observations:
          - observation_id: contigs_compatible
            predicate:
              predicate_id: genomics.snpeff.contigs_compatible.v1
              operator: boolean_equals
              expected: true
              parser_id: biomind.genomics.contig_compatibility.v1
              parser_entrypoint: agent_core.genomics_contig_parser:build_contig_compatibility_receipt
              failure_disposition: correction_required
              missing_disposition: inspection_required
              applicability:
                schema_version: 1
                kind: plan_contains_any_execution_capability
                execution_capability_ids:
                  - genomics.snpeff_annotation.prepare_database
                  - genomics.snpeff_annotation.build_database
                  - genomics.snpeff_annotation.annotate_variants
                  - genomics.snpeff_annotation.summarize_ann
                  - genomics.snpeff_annotation.finalize_outputs
            evidence_contract:
              required_fields: [value]
        workspace_mutations: []
        explicit_side_effects: []
        execution_guidance:
          - Emit contigs_compatible as a typed boolean claim. The independent structured parser belongs to the verification layer and checks the exact approved TaskSpec input paths.
          - "Do not parse VCF ##contig records with free-form grep or awk; comma-delimited metadata such as length and assembly is not part of the contig ID."
          - Review method concerns against the specific approved requirement, execution record, and independent parser receipt. Distinguish an observed violation from uncertainty; an action need not call an internal parser entrypoint unless the approved contract explicitly requires it.
          - Use the supplied concrete artifact paths explicitly; this capability has no runtime resources.
      - capability_id: genomics.snpeff_annotation.prepare_database
        operation: prepare_database
        required_runtime_binding_ids: []
        optional_runtime_binding_ids: []
        required_artifact_binding_ids: [artifact.reference_fasta, artifact.annotation_gtf]
        consumes_artifacts: [artifact.reference_fasta, artifact.annotation_gtf]
        produces_artifacts: [artifact.snpeff_config]
        produces_bindings: [genome_version, snpeff_db]
        produces_observations: [database_layout_prepared]
        workspace_mutations:
          - workspace_ref: artifact.snpeff_data_dir

# snpEff Annotation

Use this skill for VCF functional annotation with snpEff.

Aliases and trigger phrases: snpEff, SnpEff, ANN, variant effect annotation, functional annotation, build snpEff database, `genes.gff`, `genes.gtf`, `snpEff.config`.

## Core Rules

- Treat `genome-version` as the snpEff database key. It must match the `snpEff.config` entry and the data directory name, for example `data/<genome-version>/`.
- Do not infer `genome-version` from species, taxonomy, chromosome count, chromosome prefix, or a previous project.
- Prefer an official pre-built snpEff database when the exact reference build and annotation release match the user's VCF.
- Build a custom database only when the user provides the reference FASTA plus a matching annotation source such as GTF, GFF3, or GenBank.
- Require chromosome/contig names to match between VCF, FASTA, and annotation. Inspect headers before annotation when uncertain.
- Use paths visible in the shell environment where the generated Bash action will run; do not pass local desktop paths to cluster commands unless they are mounted there.
- Prefer GTF 2.2 for large eukaryotic genomes when available. Use GFF3 when that is the provided authoritative annotation. Use GenBank mainly for small genomes or when GenBank is the authoritative source.
- Treat CDS/protein consistency files as `optional_validation` for custom GTF/GFF builds. When absent, skip only the corresponding validation, record `skipped_optional_missing`, and continue; this is not an unchecked build because no required validation was skipped.
- Do not hard-code codon tables. If organellar, bacterial, plastid, mitochondrial, or other non-standard codon usage may apply, ask for or inspect the required snpEff config lines.

## Planning Contract

When custom database construction and annotation are separate plan steps, the
database directory must be declared as the capability-owned mutable workspace
`artifact.snpeff_data_dir`, not fabricated as a new immutable output artifact.
If a plan-local handle is used for allocation, its explicit resource binding
must set `canonical_resource_id: artifact.snpeff_data_dir`,
`resource_kind: mutable_workspace`, and
`contract_revision: snpeff-workspace-transition-v1`; spelling similarity is not
an alias contract. The prepare step establishes `database_layout_prepared`.
The build step requires that state, depends on prepare, and establishes
`snpeff_database_ready`. Both are ordered mutations of the same workspace, not
immutable outputs. Downstream annotation consumes that matching approved
workspace/binding identity. Do not use `mktemp` or a shell-local variable as a
cross-step carrier.
If the database is not reused across steps, build and annotate may be combined
inside one managed action.

Use the concrete Java and snpEff JAR paths supplied in the current-action
runtime context. Do not emit `$SNPEFF_JAR`, `{runtime:snpeff_jar}`, or discover
an alternative runtime inside the generated scientific action. Cross-step
semantic values are different: Generate must declare them as produced or
consumed bindings and use the exact `binding_env` variables in executable
source.

- Input/output and ANN field: `https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/inputoutput/`
- Database building: `https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/build_db/`

## Existing Database Workflow

1. Confirm that the VCF reference build equals the snpEff database build. Do not use a database just because species names match.
2. List or download databases only when network access is allowed:
   `java -jar snpEff.jar databases` or `java -jar snpEff.jar download -v <genome-version>`.
3. Annotate:
   `java -Xmx8g -jar snpEff.jar -v <genome-version> input.vcf.gz > output.snpeff.ann.vcf`.
4. Check output:
   - VCF header contains `##SnpEffVersion` and `##INFO=<ID=ANN`.
   - `snpEff_summary.html` and `snpEff_genes.txt` are produced when enabled.
   - Variants have plausible ANN fields and no systematic chromosome-not-found warnings.

## Custom Database Workflow

1. Choose a project-specific `genome-version` from the exact reference and annotation release, such as `species_ref_release`, not a broad species or taxonomy label.
2. Create a project config with:
   `<genome-version>.genome : <human-readable name>`
   plus any required codon table lines.
3. Place files in snpEff's expected layout:
   - GTF: `data/<genome-version>/genes.gtf` or `.gz`; reference FASTA as `data/genomes/<genome-version>.fa` or `data/<genome-version>/sequences.fa`.
   - GFF3: `data/<genome-version>/genes.gff` or `.gz`; reference FASTA as above unless embedded after `##FASTA`.
   - GenBank: `data/<genome-version>/genes.gbk`; concatenate multiple GenBank records only when they belong to the same reference build.
4. Build with the matching format flag: `build -gtf22`, `build -gff3`, or `build -genbank`.
5. Provide `cds.fa` and/or `protein.fa` when available. Their requirement level is `optional_validation`: when absent, the generated action disables only the unavailable check (`-noCheckCds`, `-noCheckProtein`, or both) and records `optional_validation_skipped`, the reason, and scientific limitation in approved status/report outputs, then continues. Do not ask repeatedly or promote these optional files to required. Only skipping a contract-declared required validator may be called unchecked.
6. The build subcommand must immediately follow the snpEff launcher/JAR prefix, before build-specific flags such as `-gtf22`; an `Unknown option` message that reports `Command: 'ann'` is evidence to inspect launcher/subcommand ordering, not to remove `-gtf22`.
7. Annotate the VCF only after the database build succeeds. Treat a config,
   database directory, copied `genes.gtf`/`sequences.fa`, and build log as
   partial artifacts only. The build acceptance check must verify the declared
   core predictor file `data/<genome-version>/snpEffectPredictor.bin` exists and
   is non-empty, the final build-log section has no fatal result such as
   `Database check failed`, and the database can be loaded by the same launcher
   during the annotation preflight. If any condition fails, keep the database
   stage failed/partial and do not run annotation.

Read `references/snpeff_config_templates.md` before creating a custom database config or adding any `--config-line`. It gives the supported layouts, a minimal project config, and the cases that require user confirmation.

## ANN Interpretation

- snpEff writes functional annotations to the VCF INFO `ANN` field by default.
- A single variant may have multiple ANN records because it can affect multiple transcripts, genes, or ALT alleles.
- Key ANN subfields to report: allele, effect, impact, gene name, gene ID, feature type, transcript/feature ID, biotype, exon/intron rank, HGVS.c, HGVS.p, CDS/protein positions, distance, and warnings.
- For high-impact summaries, count by `Annotation_Impact` and by Sequence Ontology effect, but keep transcript multiplicity explicit.

## Gotchas

- A matching species name is not enough; reference sequence names and coordinates must match.
- GFF3 parsing quality varies by provider. If a GTF from the same annotation release is available, prefer it for large genomes.
- If chromosome names differ only by prefixes such as `chr`, do not patch blindly. Normalize only after proving FASTA, GFF/GTF, and VCF refer to the same assembly.
- If many variants are intergenic or chromosome-not-found warnings appear, suspect a reference/annotation/VCF mismatch.
- For compressed VCF output, pipe through `bgzip` and index with `tabix` only when those tools are present.

## Extended Reference

Read `references/snpeff_notes.md` when deciding between pre-built and custom databases, explaining `genome-version`, or handling GFF/GTF/GenBank build details. Read `references/snpeff_config_templates.md` for custom config and directory-layout details.

GenomicsDB bundles, raw VCFs, and filtered VCFs must name that actual upstream
artifact; producing a different file never establishes its state. Independent
sample products may be independent resources; two writers to one mutable
identity may not be treated as independent merely because sample names differ.

This Skill declares no shared mutable-workspace lifecycle or transitions.
`artifact_kind: directory` describes a bundle's shape, not mutation permission.
Do not turn each output-file creation into a mutation of the container directory
or invent workspace state/revision strings. A real incremental shared database
needs a supported lifecycle and ordered transitions before it can be admitted.
Planning future dependencies does not claim their files already exist or pass
execution validation.

For new FASTQ preflight candidates, inspect and reuse the parent wrapper in
`genomics/wgs-short-read-mapping/scripts/inspect_fastq_batch.py`. Put its exact
bound inputs, execution-log directory and adjustable short-check deadline in
the candidate before approval. Do not hide four captured child checks until
the batch ends or forward their nested effect markers. Its stderr item events
are display facts; preserve prefix-only coverage and UNKNOWN failures. Do not
apply its 60-second initial item limit to HaplotypeCaller or other computation,
or modify a previously approved script.

Use this skill when:

- Input is coordinate-sorted, duplicate-marked WGS BAMs aligned to the same reference.
- BAMs have read groups and indexes.
- The goal is SNP/InDel discovery, usually across a cohort.
- The user wants GATK HaplotypeCaller, GVCF, GenomicsDBImport, joint genotyping, or hard filtering.

Do not use this skill for:

- RNA-seq variants; use `genomics/rnaseq-variant-calling`.
- SV/CNV; use LUMPY/CNVnator/long-read skills.
- BAMs without read groups; go back to mapping/preparation.

## 调用的参数

Required:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `REFERENCE_FASTA` | FASTA with `.fai` and `.dict` |
| `BAM_LIST` | `sample<TAB>bam_path` preferred |
| `OUTDIR` | output root |
| `INTERVALS` | chromosomes or interval TSV for large genomes |

Recommended:

| Parameter | Default / rule |
|---|---|
| `THREADS` | 4-8 per job; GATK scaling is limited |
| `MEMORY` | choose per interval and sample count |
| `TMPDIR` | fast local scratch if available |
| `JOINT_MODE` | `GenomicsDBImport` for many samples, `CombineGVCFs` for small cohorts |
| `PLOIDY` | explicit confirmed sample ploidy; unresolved means ask before calling, no implicit 2 |

Preflight:

```bash
gatk --version
test -s "${REFERENCE_FASTA}.fai"
test -s "${REFERENCE_FASTA%.*}.dict" || test -s "${REFERENCE_FASTA}.dict"
samtools quickcheck -v $(cut -f2 "${BAM_LIST}")
samtools view -H "$(cut -f2 "${BAM_LIST}" | head -1)" | grep '^@RG'
```

Core per-sample GVCF pattern:

```bash
gatk --java-options "-Xmx${MEMORY} -Djava.io.tmpdir=${TMPDIR}" HaplotypeCaller \
  -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" \
  -I "${bam}" \
  -L "${interval}" \
  --sample-ploidy "${PLOIDY:?Confirmed sample ploidy is required}" \
  -ERC GVCF \
  -O "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/gvcf/${sample}/${sample}.${interval}.g.vcf.gz"
```

Joint genotyping:

```bash
gatk GenomicsDBImport \
  --sample-name-map "gvcf.${interval}.map" \
  --genomicsdb-workspace-path "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/genomicsdb.${interval}" \
  -L "${interval}" \
  --reader-threads "${THREADS:-4}" \
  --tmp-dir "${TMPDIR}"

gatk GenotypeGVCFs \
  -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" \
  -V "gendb://${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/genomicsdb.${interval}" \
  -O "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/${interval}.raw.vcf.gz"
```

For small cohorts, `CombineGVCFs` is acceptable, but do not pass a
`sample<TAB>gvcf_path` sample map as `--variant`. `CombineGVCFs --variant`
expects each value to be an actual GVCF/VCF path. Use repeated `--variant`
arguments or a list containing only GVCF paths, then run `GenotypeGVCFs`:

```bash
gatk CombineGVCFs \
  -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" \
  --variant "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/gvcf/S1/S1.g.vcf.gz" \
  --variant "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/gvcf/S2/S2.g.vcf.gz" \
  -O "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/cohort.combined.g.vcf.gz"

gatk GenotypeGVCFs \
  -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" \
  -V "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/cohort.combined.g.vcf.gz" \
  -O "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/cohort.raw.vcf.gz"
```

Rule of thumb:

- `sample<TAB>gvcf_path` map -> `GenomicsDBImport --sample-name-map`.
- individual GVCF paths -> `CombineGVCFs --variant ... --variant ...`.
- If GATK reports a path like `S1%09/path/to/S1.g.vcf.gz`, the command passed
  a sample map where a GVCF path was expected; switch to one of the two valid
  patterns above instead of retrying the same shape.

Illustrative hard filters for a confirmed diploid short-read WGS setting only; unresolved ploidy/filter applicability requires the existing user-decision flow before use:

```bash
gatk VariantFiltration -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" -V all.raw.snp.vcf.gz \
  --filter-expression "QD < 2.0 || MQ < 40.0 || FS > 60.0 || SOR > 3.0 || MQRankSum < -12.5 || ReadPosRankSum < -8.0" \
  --filter-name SNP_filter -O all.filter.snp.vcf.gz

gatk VariantFiltration -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" -V all.raw.indel.vcf.gz \
  --filter-expression "QD < 2.0 || FS > 200.0 || SOR > 10.0 || MQRankSum < -12.5 || ReadPosRankSum < -8.0" \
  --filter-name INDEL_filter -O all.filter.indel.vcf.gz
```

Use `SelectVariants --exclude-filtered` for final PASS-only files.

## 输出结果

Expected outputs:

- `03.variant_calling/gvcf/<sample>/*.g.vcf.gz` plus indexes.
- interval raw VCFs and merged `all.raw.vcf.gz`.
- `04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz`.
- `04.filter/all.filtered.indel.vcf.gz`.
- `.tbi` or `.idx` indexes.
- `05.summary/*.bcftools.stats.txt`.
- `05.summary/variant_counts.tsv`.
- `logs/*.log`.

Validation:

```bash
gatk ValidateVariants -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" -V "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz"
gatk ValidateVariants -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" -V "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.indel.vcf.gz"
bcftools stats "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz" > "${OUTDIR}/05.summary/snp.stats.txt"
bcftools stats "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.indel.vcf.gz" > "${OUTDIR}/05.summary/indel.stats.txt"
```

Report raw and PASS counts, sample count, interval strategy, filter expressions, and ploidy.

## 常见错误及解决办法

| Problem | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| no read groups | GATK cannot track samples | fix BAM with read groups before calling |
| duplicate sample names in GVCFs | joint genotyping will fail or merge wrongly | normalize sample names and RG `SM` |
| GenomicsDB workspace already exists | rerun collision | use new workspace or remove only after user approval |
| contig mismatch | BAM/GVCF/reference differ | re-align or use matching reference |
| zero PASS variants | filters too strict or poor data | inspect raw counts and filter distribution before claiming failure |

Do not concatenate VCF text by hand. Use GATK `MergeVcfs`, Picard, or bcftools-aware tools.

# WGS bcftools SNP/InDel Calling

Use this skill for a fast short-read WGS SNP/InDel workflow. It is practical for small/medium cohorts, quick checks, and clusters without a full GATK setup.

## 确认任务边界

Use this skill when:

- Input BAMs are WGS, coordinate-sorted, indexed, and aligned to one reference.
- The user wants a lightweight caller or exploratory SNP/InDel set.
- Cohort size and compute constraints make GATK GVCF unnecessary.

Do not use this skill when:

- The user requested GATK best-practice GVCF joint genotyping.
- Input is RNA-seq; use RNA-seq variant calling.
- The target is SV or CNV.

State clearly in reports that bcftools and GATK can produce different callsets.

## 调用的参数

Required:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `REFERENCE_FASTA` | FASTA with `.fai` |
| `BAM_LIST` | one BAM path per line or `sample<TAB>bam` normalized before use |
| `OUTDIR` | output directory |

Recommended:

| Parameter | Default / notes |
|---|---|
| `THREADS` | 4-16 |
| `MIN_QUAL` | 10 for permissive first pass, tune by project |
| `REGIONS` | optional BED or region list |
| `CALL_MODE` | `--multiallelic-caller --variants-only` |

Preflight:

```bash
bcftools --version
test -s "${REFERENCE_FASTA}.fai" || samtools faidx "${REFERENCE_FASTA}"
samtools quickcheck -v $(cat "${BAM_LIST}")
```

Core call:

```bash
bcftools mpileup \
  --bam-list "${BAM_LIST}" \
  --threads "${THREADS:-8}" \
  --output-type u \
  --fasta-ref "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" |
bcftools call \
  --threads "${THREADS:-8}" \
  --multiallelic-caller \
  --variants-only \
  --output-type z \
  --output "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/all.raw.vcf.gz"
```

Basic filter and split:

```bash
bcftools filter -g 3 -G 10 -e "%QUAL<${MIN_QUAL:-10}" \
  --output-type z \
  --output "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.vcf.gz" \
  "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/all.raw.vcf.gz"

bcftools view --types snps --output-type z \
  --output "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz" \
  "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.vcf.gz"

bcftools view --types indels --output-type z \
  --output "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.indel.vcf.gz" \
  "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.vcf.gz"
```

## 输出结果

Expected outputs:

- `03.variant_calling/all.raw.vcf.gz`
- `04.filter/all.filtered.vcf.gz`
- `04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz`
- `04.filter/all.filtered.indel.vcf.gz`
- `.tbi` indexes for all compressed VCFs.
- `05.summary/*.stats.txt`
- `05.summary/variant_counts.tsv`

Validation:

```bash
for vcf in "${OUTDIR}"/03.variant_calling/all.raw.vcf.gz "${OUTDIR}"/04.filter/*.vcf.gz; do
  bcftools index -t "$vcf"
  bcftools stats "$vcf" > "${OUTDIR}/05.summary/$(basename "$vcf").stats.txt"
done
bcftools view -h "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz" >/dev/null
```

Report sample count, raw count, filtered SNP count, filtered InDel count, and filter expression.

## 常见错误及解决办法

| Problem | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `mpileup` contig mismatch | BAM and FASTA references differ | use matching FASTA or re-align |
| empty BAM list | no inputs | create normalized BAM list first |
| very large VCF or slow run | whole-genome all-sample pileup is heavy | split by chromosome/region |
| no variants after filter | filter too strict or low coverage | inspect raw VCF and depth |
| unindexed VCF | downstream stats fail | run `bcftools index -t` |

Do not call a filtered VCF "final" until it is readable, indexed, and summarized.

## Capability and failure reporting boundaries

FASTA random access (`samtools faidx`), BWA indexing (`bwa index`), sequence
dictionary creation (an explicitly verified compatible dictionary tool), and
BAM duplicate marking are different capabilities. The coarse runtime
healthcheck above is not proof of a dictionary capability: `sambamba markdup`
handles BAM duplicates and cannot replace dictionary creation. Finding an
environment directory or a command entry is not a subcommand/version check.
Use the approved runtime binding and an explicitly selected compatible tool;
never guess an environment path, silently substitute tools, or install one.
If the approved step requires a whole bundle and a required capability is
missing, accurately block. Do not automatically split the Plan or start costly
independent indexing; separate work needs existing explicit approval.

For framework evidence use the current `approved_effect_emission_template`
marker, once in a Python block before native fact values. Pass the actual
reference path as `sys.argv[1]` and observed missing entries as later argv.
After the **real** dependency check, a no-product branch can use:

tool failure retain its real rc/stderr. If publication itself fails, preserve
both the original failure and the publisher error. A directory reader refusal
does not prove corrupt data; inspect only offered readable log/evidence refs.

Use this skill to convert paired-end WGS FASTQ into duplicate-marked coordinate-sorted BAMs. The downstream caller decides whether duplicates should be marked or removed; for variant calling, default to **mark and keep**.

The versioned `generate.execution_capabilities` above is the formal effect
declaration. Use `.execute` with `operation: produce_files` for independently
produced files, `.inspect` with `operation: inspect` for observation-only checks,
and `.prepare_reference` for the declared index-producing operation. Preserve

execution authority; they are never `resource_binding` aliases for new files.

reuse that local ref in producer `outputs` and consumer `inputs`. Existing
resources must use exact current catalog references. A directory used merely

or contract revisions. A genuinely incremental mutable workflow needs an
explicit supported lifecycle/transition declaration before it can be planned.

Use this skill when:

- Input is Illumina/MGI/DNBSEQ-style paired-end WGS or resequencing FASTQ.

- The user needs reference indexes and BAM QC.

Do not use this skill when:

Before running, verify that FASTQ files are real project inputs, not tutorial/demo files.

For an approved **prefix inspection**, use this Skill's `scripts/inspect_fastq.py`
with the concrete script path obtained through Skill inspection, the exact bound
input `--path`, and an explicit `--observation-id` from the current StepEffect.
The helper uses the shared bounded inspection reader and emits the versioned
canonical observation. It does not infer identity from a value or certify full
gzip integrity, every read, or all mate pairs. Its record/input/decoded-byte/time
limits and actual coverage are part of the result. A task requiring full checks
still requires those checks; a prefix is evidence for investigation only.

For a **new FASTQ-only batch candidate**, use `scripts/inspect_fastq_batch.py`.
The correct interface is repeated `--item LABEL "BOUND_PATH"` (two arguments).
`--item "LABEL BOUND_PATH"` is invalid: never combine the label and path.
Reference FASTA does not belong in this FASTQ batch, regardless of extension.

For a step checking FASTQ **and** a reference, explicitly choose

readers and emits ONE current StepEffect `--observation-id` result, with per-item
scopes and raw logs. It never overwrites four FASTQ observations with a fifth.

byte, default header limit 4096 bytes, input limit 8192 bytes, 2 seconds. It does
not scan a long sequence line, all contigs, or the full reference; gzip reference
is explicitly unsupported by this entry. Over-limit headers remain incomplete.
FASTQ retains its existing prefix and gzip bounds; no full-file claim is valid.

Resolve these resources through the selected Skill catalog. For the composition,
declare all four handles in `skill_resources` so approval pins the wrapper and

`scripts/inspect_fasta_header.py`, `scripts/inspect_fastq_batch.py`, each prefixed
by this Skill's exact ID and `#`. Use their supplied environment handles, not
an installation root guessed from cwd. Read actual paths from current input
bindings; labels and paths are distinct shell arguments, including spaces/中文.

## 调用的参数

Required:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `REFERENCE_FASTA` | reference genome FASTA |
| `SAMPLE_TABLE` | TSV with `sample fq1 fq2` |
| `OUTDIR` | output directory |

Recommended:

| Parameter | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ALIGNER` | explicitly selected, verified compatible implementation | keep its binding and command in the approved action |
| `THREADS` | 8 or cluster-provided value | mapping and sorting |
| `SORT_MEM` | `1G` per thread | reduce on memory-limited nodes |
| `PLATFORM` | `illumina` | read group `PL` |
| `DUPLICATE_TOOL` | `picard` or `sambamba` | keep duplicates unless user asks removal |

Sample table:

```tsv
sample	fq1	fq2
S1	/path/S1_R1.fq.gz	/path/S1_R2.fq.gz
S2	/path/S2_R1.fq.gz	/path/S2_R2.fq.gz
```

Core command pattern:

```bash
bwa mem -t "${THREADS}" \
  -R "@RG\tID:${sample}\tSM:${sample}\tPL:${PLATFORM:-illumina}\tLB:${sample}\tPU:${sample}" \
  "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" "${fq1}" "${fq2}" |
samtools sort -@ "${THREADS}" -m "${SORT_MEM:-1G}" \
  -o "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.bam" -

picard MarkDuplicates \
  I="${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.bam" \
  O="${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.markdup.bam" \
  M="${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.markdup.metrics.txt" \
  CREATE_INDEX=true \
  REMOVE_DUPLICATES=false
```

Build missing reference indexes only when needed:

```bash
samtools faidx "${REFERENCE_FASTA}"
bwa index "${REFERENCE_FASTA}"
picard CreateSequenceDictionary R="${REFERENCE_FASTA}" O="${REFERENCE_FASTA%.*}.dict"
```

## 输出结果

Expected files:

- `02.mapping/<sample>.sort.markdup.bam`
- `02.mapping/<sample>.sort.markdup.bam.bai`
- `02.mapping/<sample>.markdup.metrics.txt`
- `02.mapping/<sample>.flagstat.txt`
- `02.mapping/<sample>.coverage.txt`
- `logs/<sample>.bwa.log`
- `bam.list`, preferably `sample<TAB>bam_path`

Validation:

```bash
samtools quickcheck -v "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/"*.bam
samtools view -H "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.markdup.bam" | grep '^@RG'
samtools flagstat "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.markdup.bam" > "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.flagstat.txt"
samtools coverage "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.markdup.bam" > "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.coverage.txt"
```

Report mapped percentage, properly paired percentage, duplicate rate, mean depth, and failed samples.

## 常见错误及解决办法

| Problem | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| BAM has no `@RG` | GATK sample tracking will fail | rerun with `-R` or use Picard `AddOrReplaceReadGroups` |
| `.bai` missing | downstream random access fails | run `samtools index` |
| very low mapping rate | wrong reference, contamination, poor reads | inspect FASTQ QC, reference version, sample identity |
| duplicate rate extreme | PCR/library issue or duplicated input lanes | inspect lane table and duplication metrics |
| contig mismatch later | mapping reference differs from calling reference | use one reference path/version across all stages |

Do not remove duplicates by default for WGS variant calling.

# snpEff Annotation

Use this skill for VCF functional annotation with snpEff.

Aliases and trigger phrases: snpEff, SnpEff, ANN, variant effect annotation, functional annotation, build snpEff database, `genes.gff`, `genes.gtf`, `snpEff.config`.

## Core Rules

- Treat `genome-version` as the snpEff database key. It must match the `snpEff.config` entry and the data directory name, for example `data/<genome-version>/`.
- Do not infer `genome-version` from species, taxonomy, chromosome count, chromosome prefix, or a previous project.
- Prefer an official pre-built snpEff database when the exact reference build and annotation release match the user's VCF.
- Build a custom database only when the user provides the reference FASTA plus a matching annotation source such as GTF, GFF3, or GenBank.
- Require chromosome/contig names to match between VCF, FASTA, and annotation. Inspect headers before annotation when uncertain.
- Use paths visible in the shell environment where the generated Bash action will run; do not pass local desktop paths to cluster commands unless they are mounted there.
- Prefer GTF 2.2 for large eukaryotic genomes when available. Use GFF3 when that is the provided authoritative annotation. Use GenBank mainly for small genomes or when GenBank is the authoritative source.
- Treat CDS/protein consistency files as `optional_validation` for custom GTF/GFF builds. When absent, skip only the corresponding validation, record `skipped_optional_missing`, and continue; this is not an unchecked build because no required validation was skipped.
- Do not hard-code codon tables. If organellar, bacterial, plastid, mitochondrial, or other non-standard codon usage may apply, ask for or inspect the required snpEff config lines.

## Planning Contract

When custom database construction and annotation are separate plan steps, the
database directory must be declared as the capability-owned mutable workspace
`artifact.snpeff_data_dir`, not fabricated as a new immutable output artifact.
If a plan-local handle is used for allocation, its explicit resource binding
must set `canonical_resource_id: artifact.snpeff_data_dir`,
`resource_kind: mutable_workspace`, and
`contract_revision: snpeff-workspace-transition-v1`; spelling similarity is not
an alias contract. The prepare step establishes `database_layout_prepared`.
The build step requires that state, depends on prepare, and establishes
`snpeff_database_ready`. Both are ordered mutations of the same workspace, not
immutable outputs. Downstream annotation consumes that matching approved
workspace/binding identity. Do not use `mktemp` or a shell-local variable as a
cross-step carrier.
If the database is not reused across steps, build and annotate may be combined
inside one managed action.

Use the concrete Java and snpEff JAR paths supplied in the current-action
runtime context. Do not emit `$SNPEFF_JAR`, `{runtime:snpeff_jar}`, or discover
an alternative runtime inside the generated scientific action. Cross-step
semantic values are different: Generate must declare them as produced or
consumed bindings and use the exact `binding_env` variables in executable
source.

## Official Documentation Anchors

- Running and annotation command pattern: `https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/running/`
- Input/output and ANN field: `https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/inputoutput/`
- Database building: `https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/build_db/`

## Runtime and Dependency Discovery

- Reuse `bio_gatk` for this skill. It is the shared short-read variant environment and should contain GATK/Picard plus `snpEff`; do not create a one-off `bio_snpeff` environment by default.
- Verify the declared runtime first. The skill uses `${BIO_SOURCE_INSTALL_DIR}/temurin-21` when that executable exists; it verifies the packaged `snpEff.jar` directly in the bounded `$CONDA_PREFIX/share` area. This avoids treating a broken Java launcher wrapper as proof that the installed snpEff package is absent.
- Never construct a Conda prefix by appending `anaconda3` or an environment name to the project/benchmark root. Resolve the JAR inside the verified environment, for example `SNPEFF_JAR=$(conda run -n bio_gatk bash -c 'find "$CONDA_PREFIX/share" -maxdepth 4 -type f -name snpEff.jar -print -quit')`, verify it is non-empty, and use that exact path in the Generate-owned action.
- `SNPEFF_JAVA_HOME` may override that location for one command/session, but it is not a required `.env` setting. Do not globally replace the Java used by unrelated tools.
- If the command wrapper is absent but the environment exists, search only the environment package area with a depth bound: `conda run -n bio_gatk bash -c 'find "$CONDA_PREFIX/share" -maxdepth 4 -name snpEff.jar -type f -print -quit'`.
- Never recursively scan `/`, a whole home directory, or a benchmark tree to discover `snpEff.jar` or `snpEff.config`. Never download a “latest” archive as a discovery fallback.
- If the declared check fails, delegate exactly once through `<install_tool env="bio_gatk">genomics_snpeff_annotation_runtime</install_tool>`. The installer must use the declared package contract, re-run the healthcheck, and then register the same environment. If installation is forbidden or still fails, write a truthful stage-blocked status instead of searching elsewhere.

## Generate-Owned Execution (V2)

For a V2 managed task, Generate is the sole executable action/script producer.
Use the verified runtime, TaskSpec inputs, approved Plan materializations, and
the command patterns below to create the action directly. Put every supplied
concrete input path, expected output path, Java executable path, and JAR path
directly in the action. Cross-step semantic values must use structured
`produced_bindings`, `consumed_bindings`, and `binding_env`; reuse an accepted
value exactly. Do not emit artifact placeholders or BIOMIND_INPUT/OUTPUT
variables. Do not invoke the legacy renderer and do not create or consume a
renderer manifest as V2 output authority.

## Legacy Renderer Reference (`legacy_renderer_v1` only)

The following helper examples are retained only for explicit legacy sessions
and maintainer reference. They are not active V2 routing instructions.

Render scripts for annotating with an existing database. Resolve the JAR inside the verified `bio_gatk` environment first; the renderer itself is a standard-library Python utility and should use the BioMind/current Python rather than `bio_gatk`'s Python:

```bash

test -s "$SNPEFF_JAR"
python skills/genomics/snpeff-annotation/scripts/render_snpeff_annotation_scripts.py \
  --vcf variants.vcf.gz \
  --genome-version project_or_official_database_key \
  --snpeff-jar "$SNPEFF_JAR" \
  --config /abs/path/snpEff.config \
  --outdir snpeff_annotation
```

Render scripts for building a custom GFF3 database and then annotating:

```bash
SNPEFF_JAR=$(conda run -n bio_gatk bash -c 'find "$CONDA_PREFIX/share" -maxdepth 4 -type f -name snpEff.jar -print -quit')
test -s "$SNPEFF_JAR"
python skills/genomics/snpeff-annotation/scripts/render_snpeff_annotation_scripts.py \
  --vcf variants.vcf.gz \
  --genome-version project_reference_release \
  --snpeff-jar "$SNPEFF_JAR" \
  --reference-fasta /abs/path/reference.fa \
  --annotation-gff3 /abs/path/annotation.gff3 \
  --outdir snpeff_annotation
```

For a custom GTF 2.2 database, use the renderer's real GTF interface. The
renderer adds `build -gtf22` to `02.build_database.sh`; `--gtf22`, `--gtf`,
`--fasta`, and `--output-dir` are not renderer CLI flags:

```bash

test -s "$SNPEFF_JAR"
/path/to/current/biomind/python skills/genomics/snpeff-annotation/scripts/render_snpeff_annotation_scripts.py \
  --vcf variants.vcf \
  --reference-fasta reference.fa \
  --annotation-gtf annotation.gtf \
  --genome-version project_reference_release \
  --snpeff-jar "$SNPEFF_JAR" \
  --outdir snpeff_annotation
```

Use the `controller_python` reported in the runtime context for
`/path/to/current/biomind/python`. Do not run this standard-library renderer
with `conda run -n bio_gatk python`; `bio_gatk` supplies snpEff and Java, not
the renderer interpreter.

Run each rendered script with the declared Bash runner, in manifest order. Do not derive or guess an environment prefix from the project root.

The renderer writes scripts in manifest order: `00.preflight.sh`,
`01.prepare_custom_database.sh` when custom inputs are provided,
`02.build_database.sh` for custom builds or `02.download_database.sh` for an
existing database, `03.annotate_vcf.sh`, `04.summarize_ann.sh`, and
`05.finalize.sh`. The final two scripts create the ANN effect summary and the
declared status/report/reproduction artifacts; Planner must consume these
manifest paths instead of inventing equivalent filenames.

Only an explicit `legacy_renderer_v1` session may treat the renderer's
`manifest.json` as a compatibility artifact contract. In V2, the approved Plan
and canonical output IDs remain authoritative; no manifest may rename, add, or
replace `step.outputs`.

`02.download_database.sh` requires network access and should be run only when the user has confirmed a matching official snpEff database. For offline clusters or custom references, build or point to a local database instead.

## Existing Database Workflow

1. Confirm that the VCF reference build equals the snpEff database build. Do not use a database just because species names match.
2. List or download databases only when network access is allowed:
   `java -jar snpEff.jar databases` or `java -jar snpEff.jar download -v <genome-version>`.
3. Annotate:
   `java -Xmx8g -jar snpEff.jar -v <genome-version> input.vcf.gz > output.snpeff.ann.vcf`.
4. Check output:
   - VCF header contains `##SnpEffVersion` and `##INFO=<ID=ANN`.
   - `snpEff_summary.html` and `snpEff_genes.txt` are produced when enabled.
   - Variants have plausible ANN fields and no systematic chromosome-not-found warnings.

## Custom Database Workflow

1. Choose a project-specific `genome-version` from the exact reference and annotation release, such as `species_ref_release`, not a broad species or taxonomy label.
2. Create a project config with:
   `<genome-version>.genome : <human-readable name>`
   plus any required codon table lines.
3. Place files in snpEff's expected layout:
   - GTF: `data/<genome-version>/genes.gtf` or `.gz`; reference FASTA as `data/genomes/<genome-version>.fa` or `data/<genome-version>/sequences.fa`.
   - GFF3: `data/<genome-version>/genes.gff` or `.gz`; reference FASTA as above unless embedded after `##FASTA`.
   - GenBank: `data/<genome-version>/genes.gbk`; concatenate multiple GenBank records only when they belong to the same reference build.
4. Build with the matching format flag: `build -gtf22`, `build -gff3`, or `build -genbank`.
5. Provide `cds.fa` and/or `protein.fa` when available. Their requirement level is `optional_validation`: when absent, the generated action disables only the unavailable check (`-noCheckCds`, `-noCheckProtein`, or both) and records `optional_validation_skipped`, the reason, and scientific limitation in approved status/report outputs, then continues. Do not ask repeatedly or promote these optional files to required. Only skipping a contract-declared required validator may be called unchecked.
6. The build subcommand must immediately follow the snpEff launcher/JAR prefix, before build-specific flags such as `-gtf22`; an `Unknown option` message that reports `Command: 'ann'` is evidence to inspect launcher/subcommand ordering, not to remove `-gtf22`.
7. Annotate the VCF only after the database build succeeds. Treat a config,
   database directory, copied `genes.gtf`/`sequences.fa`, and build log as
   partial artifacts only. The build acceptance check must verify the declared
   core predictor file `data/<genome-version>/snpEffectPredictor.bin` exists and
   is non-empty, the final build-log section has no fatal result such as
   `Database check failed`, and the database can be loaded by the same launcher
   during the annotation preflight. If any condition fails, keep the database
   stage failed/partial and do not run annotation.

Read `references/snpeff_config_templates.md` before creating a custom database config or adding any `--config-line`. It gives the supported layouts, a minimal project config, and the cases that require user confirmation.

## ANN Interpretation

- snpEff writes functional annotations to the VCF INFO `ANN` field by default.
- A single variant may have multiple ANN records because it can affect multiple transcripts, genes, or ALT alleles.
- Key ANN subfields to report: allele, effect, impact, gene name, gene ID, feature type, transcript/feature ID, biotype, exon/intron rank, HGVS.c, HGVS.p, CDS/protein positions, distance, and warnings.
- For high-impact summaries, count by `Annotation_Impact` and by Sequence Ontology effect, but keep transcript multiplicity explicit.

## Gotchas

- A matching species name is not enough; reference sequence names and coordinates must match.
- GFF3 parsing quality varies by provider. If a GTF from the same annotation release is available, prefer it for large genomes.
- If chromosome names differ only by prefixes such as `chr`, do not patch blindly. Normalize only after proving FASTA, GFF/GTF, and VCF refer to the same assembly.
- If many variants are intergenic or chromosome-not-found warnings appear, suspect a reference/annotation/VCF mismatch.
- For compressed VCF output, pipe through `bgzip` and index with `tabix` only when those tools are present.

## Extended Reference

Read `references/snpeff_notes.md` when deciding between pre-built and custom databases, explaining `genome-version`, or handling GFF/GTF/GenBank build details. Read `references/snpeff_config_templates.md` for custom config and directory-layout details.

# WGS GATK SNP/InDel Calling

Use this skill for the GATK best-practice style short-read WGS GVCF workflow. In schema-2, Generate owns the current approved action. Consult `genomics/wgs-variant-calling` for interval planning and documented interfaces; do not assume a legacy helper supplies an unresolved biological parameter.

## Formal planning contract

The versioned `generate.execution_capabilities` above is the formal effect
declaration. Use `.execute` with `operation: produce_files` for new file/bundle
products and `.inspect` with `operation: inspect` for observation-only checks.
Retain HaplotypeCaller, joint genotyping, filtering, and other scientific choices
in the existing title and success_criteria, with user decisions carried from the canonical task. An execution
capability ID is not a resource identity or an alias for its output files.

Assign each new file or one-shot GenomicsDB bundle its own candidate-local ref,
with one producer and explicit consumer dependencies. Reads of combined GVCFs,
GenomicsDB bundles, raw VCFs, and filtered VCFs must name that actual upstream
artifact; producing a different file never establishes its state. Independent
sample products may be independent resources; two writers to one mutable
identity may not be treated as independent merely because sample names differ.

This Skill declares no shared mutable-workspace lifecycle or transitions.
`artifact_kind: directory` describes a bundle's shape, not mutation permission.
Do not turn each output-file creation into a mutation of the container directory
or invent workspace state/revision strings. A real incremental shared database
needs a supported lifecycle and ordered transitions before it can be admitted.
Planning future dependencies does not claim their files already exist or pass
execution validation.

## 确认任务边界

For new FASTQ preflight candidates, inspect and reuse the parent wrapper in
`genomics/wgs-short-read-mapping/scripts/inspect_fastq_batch.py`. Put its exact
bound inputs, execution-log directory and adjustable short-check deadline in
the candidate before approval. Do not hide four captured child checks until
the batch ends or forward their nested effect markers. Its stderr item events
are display facts; preserve prefix-only coverage and UNKNOWN failures. Do not
apply its 60-second initial item limit to HaplotypeCaller or other computation,
or modify a previously approved script.

Use this skill when:

- Input is coordinate-sorted, duplicate-marked WGS BAMs aligned to the same reference.
- BAMs have read groups and indexes.
- The goal is SNP/InDel discovery, usually across a cohort.
- The user wants GATK HaplotypeCaller, GVCF, GenomicsDBImport, joint genotyping, or hard filtering.

Do not use this skill for:

- RNA-seq variants; use `genomics/rnaseq-variant-calling`.
- SV/CNV; use LUMPY/CNVnator/long-read skills.
- BAMs without read groups; go back to mapping/preparation.

Confirm sample ploidy before HaplotypeCaller when the user prohibits guessing
critical scientific parameters. Preserve an unknown value in Consultant's
existing unresolved handoff and the same Plan's ask_user dependency. Input
checks and mapping need not wait, but calling/filter decisions that depend on
this value must wait for the existing user-decision flow. General Plan approval
is not biological confirmation. Use only the answer interpreted through the
existing confirm_decision evidence; never infer from names or species labels.

## 调用的参数

Required:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `REFERENCE_FASTA` | FASTA with `.fai` and `.dict` |
| `BAM_LIST` | `sample<TAB>bam_path` preferred |
| `OUTDIR` | output root |
| `INTERVALS` | chromosomes or interval TSV for large genomes |

Recommended:

| Parameter | Default / rule |
|---|---|
| `THREADS` | 4-8 per job; GATK scaling is limited |
| `MEMORY` | choose per interval and sample count |
| `TMPDIR` | fast local scratch if available |
| `JOINT_MODE` | `GenomicsDBImport` for many samples, `CombineGVCFs` for small cohorts |
| `PLOIDY` | explicit confirmed sample ploidy; unresolved means ask before calling, no implicit 2 |

Preflight:

```bash
gatk --version
test -s "${REFERENCE_FASTA}.fai"
test -s "${REFERENCE_FASTA%.*}.dict" || test -s "${REFERENCE_FASTA}.dict"
samtools quickcheck -v $(cut -f2 "${BAM_LIST}")
samtools view -H "$(cut -f2 "${BAM_LIST}" | head -1)" | grep '^@RG'
```

Core per-sample GVCF pattern:

```bash
gatk --java-options "-Xmx${MEMORY} -Djava.io.tmpdir=${TMPDIR}" HaplotypeCaller \
  -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" \
  -I "${bam}" \
  -L "${interval}" \
  --sample-ploidy "${PLOIDY:?Confirmed sample ploidy is required}" \
  -ERC GVCF \
  -O "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/gvcf/${sample}/${sample}.${interval}.g.vcf.gz"
```

Joint genotyping:

```bash
gatk GenomicsDBImport \
  --sample-name-map "gvcf.${interval}.map" \
  --genomicsdb-workspace-path "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/genomicsdb.${interval}" \
  -L "${interval}" \
  --reader-threads "${THREADS:-4}" \
  --tmp-dir "${TMPDIR}"

gatk GenotypeGVCFs \
  -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" \
  -V "gendb://${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/genomicsdb.${interval}" \
  -O "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/${interval}.raw.vcf.gz"
```

For small cohorts, `CombineGVCFs` is acceptable, but do not pass a
`sample<TAB>gvcf_path` sample map as `--variant`. `CombineGVCFs --variant`
expects each value to be an actual GVCF/VCF path. Use repeated `--variant`
arguments or a list containing only GVCF paths, then run `GenotypeGVCFs`:

```bash
gatk CombineGVCFs \
  -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" \
  --variant "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/gvcf/S1/S1.g.vcf.gz" \
  --variant "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/gvcf/S2/S2.g.vcf.gz" \
  -O "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/cohort.combined.g.vcf.gz"

gatk GenotypeGVCFs \
  -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" \
  -V "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/cohort.combined.g.vcf.gz" \
  -O "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/cohort.raw.vcf.gz"
```

Rule of thumb:

- `sample<TAB>gvcf_path` map -> `GenomicsDBImport --sample-name-map`.
- individual GVCF paths -> `CombineGVCFs --variant ... --variant ...`.
- If GATK reports a path like `S1%09/path/to/S1.g.vcf.gz`, the command passed
  a sample map where a GVCF path was expected; switch to one of the two valid
  patterns above instead of retrying the same shape.

Illustrative hard filters for a confirmed diploid short-read WGS setting only; unresolved ploidy/filter applicability requires the existing user-decision flow before use:

```bash
gatk VariantFiltration -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" -V all.raw.snp.vcf.gz \
  --filter-expression "QD < 2.0 || MQ < 40.0 || FS > 60.0 || SOR > 3.0 || MQRankSum < -12.5 || ReadPosRankSum < -8.0" \
  --filter-name SNP_filter -O all.filter.snp.vcf.gz

gatk VariantFiltration -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" -V all.raw.indel.vcf.gz \
  --filter-expression "QD < 2.0 || FS > 200.0 || SOR > 10.0 || MQRankSum < -12.5 || ReadPosRankSum < -8.0" \
  --filter-name INDEL_filter -O all.filter.indel.vcf.gz
```

Use `SelectVariants --exclude-filtered` for final PASS-only files.

## 输出结果

Expected outputs:

- `03.variant_calling/gvcf/<sample>/*.g.vcf.gz` plus indexes.
- interval raw VCFs and merged `all.raw.vcf.gz`.
- `04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz`.
- `04.filter/all.filtered.indel.vcf.gz`.
- `.tbi` or `.idx` indexes.
- `05.summary/*.bcftools.stats.txt`.
- `05.summary/variant_counts.tsv`.
- `logs/*.log`.

Validation:

```bash
gatk ValidateVariants -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" -V "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz"
gatk ValidateVariants -R "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" -V "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.indel.vcf.gz"
bcftools stats "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz" > "${OUTDIR}/05.summary/snp.stats.txt"
bcftools stats "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.indel.vcf.gz" > "${OUTDIR}/05.summary/indel.stats.txt"
```

Report raw and PASS counts, sample count, interval strategy, filter expressions, and ploidy.

## 常见错误及解决办法

| Problem | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| no read groups | GATK cannot track samples | fix BAM with read groups before calling |
| duplicate sample names in GVCFs | joint genotyping will fail or merge wrongly | normalize sample names and RG `SM` |
| GenomicsDB workspace already exists | rerun collision | use new workspace or remove only after user approval |
| contig mismatch | BAM/GVCF/reference differ | re-align or use matching reference |
| zero PASS variants | filters too strict or poor data | inspect raw counts and filter distribution before claiming failure |

Do not concatenate VCF text by hand. Use GATK `MergeVcfs`, Picard, or bcftools-aware tools.

## 相似的 skills

- `genomics/wgs-variant-calling` - related interfaces and interval planning; legacy renderer examples do not supply unresolved parameters.
- `genomics/wgs-short-read-mapping` - prepare BAMs from FASTQ.
- `genomics/wgs-bcftools-snp-indel` - faster lightweight SNP/InDel workflow.
- `genomics/rnaseq-variant-calling` - RNA-seq variant workflow.
- `genomics/snpeff-annotation` - annotate final VCF.

# WGS bcftools SNP/InDel Calling

Use this skill for a fast short-read WGS SNP/InDel workflow. It is practical for small/medium cohorts, quick checks, and clusters without a full GATK setup.

## 确认任务边界

Use this skill when:

- Input BAMs are WGS, coordinate-sorted, indexed, and aligned to one reference.
- The user wants a lightweight caller or exploratory SNP/InDel set.
- Cohort size and compute constraints make GATK GVCF unnecessary.

Do not use this skill when:

- The user requested GATK best-practice GVCF joint genotyping.
- Input is RNA-seq; use RNA-seq variant calling.
- The target is SV or CNV.

State clearly in reports that bcftools and GATK can produce different callsets.

## 调用的参数

Required:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `REFERENCE_FASTA` | FASTA with `.fai` |
| `BAM_LIST` | one BAM path per line or `sample<TAB>bam` normalized before use |
| `OUTDIR` | output directory |

Recommended:

| Parameter | Default / notes |
|---|---|
| `THREADS` | 4-16 |
| `MIN_QUAL` | 10 for permissive first pass, tune by project |
| `REGIONS` | optional BED or region list |
| `CALL_MODE` | `--multiallelic-caller --variants-only` |

Preflight:

```bash
bcftools --version
test -s "${REFERENCE_FASTA}.fai" || samtools faidx "${REFERENCE_FASTA}"
samtools quickcheck -v $(cat "${BAM_LIST}")
```

Core call:

```bash
bcftools mpileup \
  --bam-list "${BAM_LIST}" \
  --threads "${THREADS:-8}" \
  --output-type u \
  --fasta-ref "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" |
bcftools call \
  --threads "${THREADS:-8}" \
  --multiallelic-caller \
  --variants-only \
  --output-type z \
  --output "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/all.raw.vcf.gz"
```

Basic filter and split:

```bash
bcftools filter -g 3 -G 10 -e "%QUAL<${MIN_QUAL:-10}" \
  --output-type z \
  --output "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.vcf.gz" \
  "${OUTDIR}/03.variant_calling/all.raw.vcf.gz"

bcftools view --types snps --output-type z \
  --output "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz" \
  "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.vcf.gz"

bcftools view --types indels --output-type z \
  --output "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.indel.vcf.gz" \
  "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.vcf.gz"
```

## 输出结果

Expected outputs:

- `03.variant_calling/all.raw.vcf.gz`
- `04.filter/all.filtered.vcf.gz`
- `04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz`
- `04.filter/all.filtered.indel.vcf.gz`
- `.tbi` indexes for all compressed VCFs.
- `05.summary/*.stats.txt`
- `05.summary/variant_counts.tsv`

Validation:

```bash
for vcf in "${OUTDIR}"/03.variant_calling/all.raw.vcf.gz "${OUTDIR}"/04.filter/*.vcf.gz; do
  bcftools index -t "$vcf"
  bcftools stats "$vcf" > "${OUTDIR}/05.summary/$(basename "$vcf").stats.txt"
done
bcftools view -h "${OUTDIR}/04.filter/all.filtered.snp.vcf.gz" >/dev/null
```

Report sample count, raw count, filtered SNP count, filtered InDel count, and filter expression.

## 常见错误及解决办法

| Problem | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `mpileup` contig mismatch | BAM and FASTA references differ | use matching FASTA or re-align |
| empty BAM list | no inputs | create normalized BAM list first |
| very large VCF or slow run | whole-genome all-sample pileup is heavy | split by chromosome/region |
| no variants after filter | filter too strict or low coverage | inspect raw VCF and depth |
| unindexed VCF | downstream stats fail | run `bcftools index -t` |

Do not call a filtered VCF "final" until it is readable, indexed, and summarized.

# WGS Short-Read Mapping

## Capability and failure reporting boundaries

FASTA random access (`samtools faidx`), BWA indexing (`bwa index`), sequence
dictionary creation (an explicitly verified compatible dictionary tool), and
BAM duplicate marking are different capabilities. The coarse runtime
healthcheck above is not proof of a dictionary capability: `sambamba markdup`
handles BAM duplicates and cannot replace dictionary creation. Finding an
environment directory or a command entry is not a subcommand/version check.
Use the approved runtime binding and an explicitly selected compatible tool;
never guess an environment path, silently substitute tools, or install one.
If the approved step requires a whole bundle and a required capability is
missing, accurately block. Do not automatically split the Plan or start costly
independent indexing; separate work needs existing explicit approval.

For framework evidence use the current `approved_effect_emission_template`
marker, once in a Python block before native fact values. Pass the actual
reference path as `sys.argv[1]` and observed missing entries as later argv.

## 确认任务边界

Use this skill when:

- Input is Illumina/MGI/DNBSEQ-style paired-end WGS or resequencing FASTQ.
- The next stage is WGS SNP/InDel, Manta short-read SV, or CNVnator CNV.
- The user needs reference indexes and BAM QC.

Do not use this skill when:

- Reads are RNA-seq; use `genomics/rnaseq-variant-calling`.
- Reads are ONT/PacBio long reads; use `genomics/long-read-sv-sniffles2`.
- BAMs are already aligned, coordinate-sorted, indexed, and have read groups; go directly to the caller.

Before running, verify that FASTQ files are real project inputs, not tutorial/demo files.

For an approved **prefix inspection**, use this Skill's `scripts/inspect_fastq.py`
with the concrete script path obtained through Skill inspection, the exact bound
input `--path`, and an explicit `--observation-id` from the current StepEffect.
The helper uses the shared bounded inspection reader and emits the versioned
canonical observation. It does not infer identity from a value or certify full
gzip integrity, every read, or all mate pairs. Its record/input/decoded-byte/time
limits and actual coverage are part of the result. A task requiring full checks
still requires those checks; a prefix is evidence for investigation only.

For a **new FASTQ-only batch candidate**, use `scripts/inspect_fastq_batch.py`.
The correct interface is repeated `--item LABEL "BOUND_PATH"` (two arguments).
`--item "LABEL BOUND_PATH"` is invalid: never combine the label and path.
Reference FASTA does not belong in this FASTQ batch, regardless of extension.

For a step checking FASTQ **and** a reference, explicitly choose
`scripts/inspect_wgs_inputs.py`: repeat `--fastq LABEL "BOUND_PATH"`, then pass
`--reference LABEL "BOUND_PATH"`. This thin composition delegates to the two
readers and emits ONE current StepEffect `--observation-id` result, with per-item
scopes and raw logs. It never overwrites four FASTQ observations with a fifth.
`scripts/inspect_fasta_header.py` checks plain UTF-8 FASTA header and one sequence
byte, default header limit 4096 bytes, input limit 8192 bytes, 2 seconds. It does
not scan a long sequence line, all contigs, or the full reference; gzip reference
is explicitly unsupported by this entry. Over-limit headers remain incomplete.
FASTQ retains its existing prefix and gzip bounds; no full-file claim is valid.

## 调用的参数

Required:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `REFERENCE_FASTA` | reference genome FASTA |
| `SAMPLE_TABLE` | TSV with `sample fq1 fq2` |
| `OUTDIR` | output directory |

Recommended:

| Parameter | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ALIGNER` | explicitly selected, verified compatible implementation | keep its binding and command in the approved action |
| `THREADS` | 8 or cluster-provided value | mapping and sorting |
| `SORT_MEM` | `1G` per thread | reduce on memory-limited nodes |
| `PLATFORM` | `illumina` | read group `PL` |
| `DUPLICATE_TOOL` | `picard` or `sambamba` | keep duplicates unless user asks removal |

Sample table:

```tsv
sample	fq1	fq2
S1	/path/S1_R1.fq.gz	/path/S1_R2.fq.gz
S2	/path/S2_R1.fq.gz	/path/S2_R2.fq.gz
```

Core command pattern:

```bash
bwa mem -t "${THREADS}" \
  -R "@RG\tID:${sample}\tSM:${sample}\tPL:${PLATFORM:-illumina}\tLB:${sample}\tPU:${sample}" \
  "${REFERENCE_FASTA}" "${fq1}" "${fq2}" |
samtools sort -@ "${THREADS}" -m "${SORT_MEM:-1G}" \
  -o "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.bam" -

picard MarkDuplicates \
  I="${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.bam" \
  O="${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.markdup.bam" \
  M="${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.markdup.metrics.txt" \
  CREATE_INDEX=true \
  REMOVE_DUPLICATES=false
```

Build missing reference indexes only when needed:

```bash
samtools faidx "${REFERENCE_FASTA}"
bwa index "${REFERENCE_FASTA}"
picard CreateSequenceDictionary R="${REFERENCE_FASTA}" O="${REFERENCE_FASTA%.*}.dict"
```

Expected files:

- `02.mapping/<sample>.sort.markdup.bam`
- `02.mapping/<sample>.sort.markdup.bam.bai`
- `02.mapping/<sample>.markdup.metrics.txt`
- `02.mapping/<sample>.flagstat.txt`
- `02.mapping/<sample>.coverage.txt`
- `logs/<sample>.bwa.log`

Validation:

```bash
samtools quickcheck -v "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/"*.bam
samtools view -H "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.markdup.bam" | grep '^@RG'
samtools flagstat "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.markdup.bam" > "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.flagstat.txt"
samtools coverage "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.sort.markdup.bam" > "${OUTDIR}/02.mapping/${sample}.coverage.txt"
```

Report mapped percentage, properly paired percentage, duplicate rate, mean depth, and failed samples.

## 常见错误及解决办法

| Problem | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| BAM has no `@RG` | GATK sample tracking will fail | rerun with `-R` or use Picard `AddOrReplaceReadGroups` |
| `.bai` missing | downstream random access fails | run `samtools index` |
| very low mapping rate | wrong reference, contamination, poor reads | inspect FASTQ QC, reference version, sample identity |
| duplicate rate extreme | PCR/library issue or duplicated input lanes | inspect lane table and duplication metrics |
| contig mismatch later | mapping reference differs from calling reference | use one reference path/version across all stages |

Do not remove duplicates by default for WGS variant calling.
